key_insight: A multi-branch shell model shows that adding branching geometry to quasi-local cascade dynamics increases intermittency and strengthens anomalous scaling in turbulent energy transfer.
engineering_relevance: This suggests reduced turbulence models and subgrid ideas should capture not only nonlinear interactions but also the cascade’s geometric organization to better predict rare, intense events.
method: Built a multi-branch shell model combining quasi-local triadic interactions with a branching structure toward small scales.
Compared intermittency statistics against the standard Sabra shell model.
Analyzed multiplier statistics and large-deviation behavior of energy-flux structure functions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative measurements of anomalous scaling exponents and flux statistics, showing stronger intermittency in the branching model than in Sabra.
watch_item: Shell models simplify Navier–Stokes turbulence, so the branching-enhanced intermittency may not transfer quantitatively without validation in full 3D flows.
paper_title: Intermittency in Shell Models of Turbulent Cascades: from Single-Branch to Multi-Branch
